s: Hi Becca.
你好，贝卡。
Phil
Hi Phil.
您好，菲尔。
Becca
Becca, I've got a question for you.
贝卡，我想问你一个问题。
Phil
What's the last plastic thing you had in your hands?
你手里最后的塑料是什么？
Well, I just did my makeup, so probably a makeup brush.
我刚刚做了化品，所以可能是化刷。
Becca
Many of us own lots of things made of plastic.
我们有很多塑料制成的东西。
Phil
It's cheap, easy to shape and long lasting, but that's not always a good thing.
它便宜，容易塑造，持久，但这并不总是好事。
In this episode of 6 Minute English, we'll be hearing from experts as they teach us about microplastics – those are tiny plastic pieces.
在"六分钟英语"的节目中，我们会听到专家们教导我们关于微塑料。
And we'll be asking the question, 'Are microplastics affecting our health?'
我们会问"，微塑料是否影响我们的健康？"
OK.
没有问题。
Well, let's start with our quiz, Becca.
让我们开始试题，贝卡。
There was a social media post that says that every week we ingest the same amount of plastic as there is in a credit card, but that's not true.
社交媒体上的一篇文章说，每周，我们摄入的塑料量与信用卡的相同，但这不是真的。
Oh, thank goodness!
谢天谢地！
Becca
So, my question for you is how long would it really take to ingest that amount of microplastics?
所以，我的问题是，真正需要多长时间才能摄入那么多的微塑料？
Phil
Would it be: a) 13,000 years, b) 23,000 years, or c) 33,000 years?
Well, I want to be hopeful, so I'll go with the longest period of time.
我想要充满希望，所以我会选择最长的时间。
Becca
That would be 33,000 years.
OK.
没有问题。
Phil
Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
我们将在节目结束时找到答案。
So, the World Health Organisation says that microplastics have been found in many different food groups.
世界卫生组织说，微塑料已经在许多不同的食物群体中被发现。
Becca
But Phil, what is the food group that is more affected by microplastics?
但菲尔，哪些食物群体受到微塑料的影响更大？
Well, scientists have found that seafood is one of the main food groups where microplastics can be found, and BBC World Service programme The Evidence has been investigating this.
科学家发现海鲜是微塑料的主要食物群体之一，证据一直在调查这个问题。
Phil
Professor Shilpa Chokshi told host Claudia Hammond about some pictures that she was shown by a microplastics expert.
教授Shilpa Chokshi告诉主持人Claudia Hammond她被微塑料专家展示的一些照片。
And he showed me all these marine animals that looked like they had plastics in their livers and hind guts.
他向我展示了所有的海洋动物，看起来像它们的肝脏和后肠中有塑料。
Professor Shilpa Chokshi

And from that initial discussion, I went away and I looked at the literature and I looked at the data, and there was emerging evidence that there was plastics in the liver, and there was this correlation increase.
从最初的讨论开始，我走了，看了文献，看了数据，有证据表明，肝脏中有塑料，这种相关性增加了。
Shilpa says that plastics have been found in marine animals.
希尔帕说，海洋动物中发现了塑料。
Becca
Marine describes anything related to, found in or produced by the sea.
海洋描述与海洋有关，发现或产生的任何东西。
Yes, these pictures of marine animals with plastics in their bodies inspired Shilpa to dive deeper into the data.
是的，这些有塑料的海洋动物的照片激发了希尔帕深入研究数据。
Phil
She found emerging evidence, and the adjective emerging describes something coming into view after being hidden, allowing it to develop or be better understood.
她发现了新的证据，而出现的形容词描述了隐藏后出现的东西，允许它发展或更好地理解。
And from this emerging evidence, Shilpa noticed a correlation .
而从这些新兴证据中，希尔帕注意到了相关性。
Becca
You'll hear this word a lot when talking about data.
在谈论数据时，你会经常听到这个词。
A correlation is a link or connection between two or more things.
关联是两个或多个东西之间的联系。
So, Phil, we know how toxic microplastics get into our body, but are they definitely harmful?
所以，菲尔，我们知道有毒的微塑料如何进入我们的身体，但它们确实是有害的吗？。
Well, plastics have been a big part of daily life since the 1950s, but it's only recently that we've started thinking about microplastics as a health issue.
自20世纪50年代以来，塑料一直是日常生活的重要组成部分，但直到最近才开始将微塑料视为健康问题。
Phil
For example, scientists have been looking at people who worked in nylon factories where they were exposed to high levels of microplastic.
例如，科学家们一直在研究那些在尼龙工厂工作的人，
And the scientists think that there may be a correlation between this and diseases that they developed later on.
科学家们认为，这可能与他们后来发展的疾病之间存在相关性。
Science professor Mark Miodownik, from University College London, has mixed feelings about microplastics and explained these to BBC World Service programme The Evidence.
科学教授马克·米奥多尼克，从伦敦大学学院，他对微塑料有不同的感觉，并向BBC世界服务节目"证据"解释了这些。
Well, you know, we have been exposed for decades and surely if it was that bad, you know, we'd have seen a spike or something by now.
好吧，你知道的，我们已经暴露了几十年，你知道的，到现在，我们会看到一个尖或类似的东西。
Professor Mark Miodownik
But on the other hand, you know, I think, you know, if you look at how much plastic packaging is in supermarkets, it's gone up and up and up and up.
但另一方面，你知道的，我认为，你知道，如果你看看超市里有多少塑料包装，它已经上升，上升，上升，上升。
And this is not a quantified measure, but our exposure seems to be increasing, and that's the worry for me.
这不是一个量化的测量，但我们的暴露似乎正在增加，这是我最担心的。
Mark mentions that some people say if microplastics were harmful, we surely would have seen a spike in issues related to them by now.
马克提到一些人说，如果微塑料是有害的，目前，我们肯定会看到与它们有关的问题升。
Becca
A spike is literally a pointy shape, but here it means a sudden, sharp increase in something.
一个尖字面上是一个尖的形状，但在这里，它意味着某种东西突然，急剧增加。
Right.
很好。
Phil
And though the amount of plastic packaging we use has increased, this isn't a quantified measure.
尽管我们使用的塑料包装量增加了，但这并不是一个量化的指标。
If something is quantified , then it's measured and given a number or a value.
如果某种东西被量化，那么它被测量并得到一个数字或值。
So, Mark concludes that he is worried about our exposure to plastics.
因此，马克得出结论，他担心我们的接触塑料。
Becca
Exposure means coming into contact with something that may have an impact on you.
暴露意味着接触到可能影响你的东西。
OK.
没有问题。
Phil, so, if people are worried about their exposure to microplastics, what can they do to reduce this?
菲尔，如果人们担心他们对微塑料的接触，他们能做些什么来减少这一点？
Well, one thing they can do is to replace things like plastic chopping boards, utensils and food storage containers.
它们可以替换塑料切割板，器具和食品储存容器等。
Phil
And another tip from BBC World Service's The Evidence is to replace tea bags, which often contain microplastics, with loose-leaf tea.
而BBC世界服务部"证据"的另一个建议是用松叶茶取代经常含有微塑料的茶袋。
OK.
没有问题。
Becca, now it's time to get the answer to our quiz question.
贝卡，现在是时候回答我们的问卷问题了。
And I asked you how long it would take to ingest a credit-card-sized amount of microplastics.
我问你需要多长时间才能吸收一个信用卡大小的微塑料。
Yes, and I said 33,000 years.
Becca
OK.
没有问题。
Phil
Well, I've got two bits of bad news for you, Becca.
我有两个坏消息给你，贝卡。
One, you were wrong.
一，你错了。
And two, I'm afraid it's only 23,000 years that it would take to ingest that plastic.
第二，我担心只需要23000年才能消耗塑料。
OK.
没有问题。
Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with marine , which describes anything related to, found in or produced by the sea.
让我们回顾我们在这个节目中学到的词汇，从海军开始，描述任何与此相关的东西，在海洋中发现或产生的。
The adjective emerging describes something coming into view after being hidden, allowing it to develop or be better understood.
出现的形容词描述了被隐藏后出现的东西，让它发展或更好地理解。
Becca
A correlation is a relationship between two or more things.
关联是两个或多个东西之间的关系。
Phil
A spike is a sudden, sharp increase in something.
一个杆是什么东西的突然，急剧增加。
Becca
If something is quantified , it's measured and given a number or a value.
如果某种东西被定量化，它被测量并得到一个数字或值。
Phil
And exposure means to come into contact with something that may have an impact on you.
暴露意味着接触到可能影响你的东西。
Becca
Once again, our six minutes are up.
再一次，我们的六分钟已经过去了。
Phil
Test what you've learned with the worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
通过我们的网站，bbclearningenglish.com,

w.correlation: n. 相互关系，相关，关联
w.marine: n. 舰队，水兵，海景画；a. 海的，海产的，海底的
w.quantified: vt. 定量，用数量表示，测量
w.spike: n. 长钉，鞋钉，钉状物；vt. 以大钉钉牢，用尖物刺穿，阻止
w.utensils: n. 器具，用具，器皿( utensil的名词复数 )
w.adjective: n. 形容词；a. 形容词的，从属的
w.recap: vt. 翻新胎面；n. 翻新的轮胎
w.hind: n. 雌鹿；a. 后部的，在后的
